# R113 — Persistent atom–rank index for exact all-k capacity under single-sided source edits

Date: 2026-11-13 (Asia/Shanghai). Role: author-side mathematical research, auxiliary rational S23 directed-circle model. Independent review: pending. Formal Task CLAIM: not established.

Frozen scientific input: `43ec6098b1330ae86d0a7863be336c5d97f6ef34`. Direct predecessor: R112 `research_notes/brc_s23_av_r112_first_difference_capacity_20261113/PROOF.md` at immutable commit `6002ed45539c4e3112ec3c41a60a901604792eb9`. Results below apply to the explicitly typed auxiliary rank/membership model; no native six-dimensional Heartbeat realization is inferred.

## 1. Problem and definitions

Let `U=(u_0 ≻ u_1 ≻ ... ≻ u_{n-1})` be a finite immutable universe of **distinct complete source identities**. Fix any parameter domain `I` with a finite exact partition into `q` atoms `J_0,...,J_{q-1}`, on each of which every source eligibility predicate `M_u(θ)` is constant. Every singleton crossing is an atom in its own right. A source version is a set `F⊆U`. The descending eligible tuple is `Top_k(F,θ)`, truncated to `k` or the available length.

For versions `F,G` define `C=F∩G`, `Δ=F△G`. At atom `J` and rank index `i` define two 0/1 bits:

`c_i(J)=1[u_i∈C] 1[M_{u_i}(J)]`, `d_i(J)=1[u_i∈Δ] 1[M_{u_i}(J)]`.

An immutable binary rank tree over `[0,n-1]` stores `C(v)=Σ c_i`, `D(v)=Σ d_i` for each subtree, with each leaf preserving its exact source rank/identity. The rank tree root is stored in each leaf of a second immutable binary **atom tree** indexed by the exact parameter atoms; an internal atom node stores the minimum capacity among descendants, with `∞` as a tagged value when no differing eligible source exists.

This is a persistence architecture for a **fixed, known finite source universe and atom partition**. New times or new crossing points require exact refinement, e.g. using R111/R112, before the fixed-partition update theorem below applies.

## 2. Theorem R113.1 — O(log n) rank-prefix recovery at one parameter atom

At any atom `J` let `i^*(J)=min{i:d_i(J)=1}` if a difference is eligible. The first-difference capacity is

`h(J)=Σ_{i<i^*} c_i(J)`, and `h(J)=∞` when all `d_i(J)=0`.

Algorithm: starting at the rank root, always descend left if the left subtree has `D>0`; otherwise add the left subtree's `C` to a prefix accumulator and descend right. If the root `D=0`, return `∞`. Upon reaching the first positive-difference leaf, output the accumulated common count. The descent takes `O(log(n+1))` node visits for a balanced segment tree, excluding arbitrary-precision integer bit costs.

**Proof.** The left subtree contains precisely the higher-ranked half. If it contains any differing eligible identity, the earliest difference must lie there and every skipped common identity has rank no higher than the first difference. Otherwise no difference lies there, so all its `C` eligible common identities belong to the identical prefix of both versions and can be counted at once. Repeat inductively. At the selected leaf, the accumulated count equals the number of eligible common identities strictly above the highest eligible differing identity. By R112's first-difference theorem, the first divergent rank of the full two source lists is exactly `h(J)+1`. When `D=0`, all eligible identities coincide. ∎

## 3. Theorem R113.2 — Persistent exact all-k certificate and local edits

Let `K^*(I)=min_{0≤i<q}h(J_i)` in `ℕ∪{∞}`. Then for **every integer `k≥1`**,

`(∀θ∈I, Top_k(F,θ)=Top_k(G,θ)) ⇔ k≤K^*(I)`.

The atom-tree root stores `K^*(I)` directly. If it is finite, descending to any leaf attaining the minimum returns an atom `J^*` and its exact rational representative `θ^*`; this same representative witnesses inequivalence for **all `k>K^*(I)`**.

Now toggle one complete identity `u` in exactly one of the versions `F,G`. Its time/membership predicate is unchanged. Let `A_u={i:M_u(J_i)=1}` and `a=|A_u|`. For every `i∉A_u`, the rank-tree and atom-tree leaf are unchanged and **the old immutable subtree may be reused**. For every `i∈A_u`, update only the rank leaf for `u` to the new pair `(c_i,d_i)`, reconstruct its `O(log(n+1))` rank-tree path, recover the new `h(J_i)` by Theorem R113.1, and replace the `O(log(q+1))` atom-tree path. Older roots remain valid for branching histories.

With indexed `A_u` and precomputed exact atoms, a single edit requires

`O(a(log(n+1)+log(q+1)))` segment-tree node visits and new persistent nodes, plus integer arithmetic on counters, source-set operations and exact source-membership precomputation. A global all-k equivalence threshold is read from the root in `O(1)`, and a rational minimal-disagreement witness is recovered by one atom-tree descent in `O(log(q+1))`, aside from output representation costs.

**Proof.** A one-sided membership toggle changes the `(C,Δ)` ownership of exactly one complete identity. At an ineligible parameter atom both counts remain zero, hence the entire rank tree is unchanged. At an eligible atom only one rank leaf changes; subtree sums on unaffected paths are identical. Functional path copying preserves old trees. Theorem R113.1 recomputes the new capacity exactly, and inductive minima on the outer tree give the minimum over all atoms. On every exact atom the list eligibility is constant, including singleton boundary atoms; applying R112 to all atoms proves the equivalence threshold and witness assertion. Balanced trees give the stated path lengths. ∎

**Accounting and scope.** The initial exact atomization, eligibility inversion `A_u`, initial rank trees and any new-cut refinements have separate costs. The present reference checker deliberately materializes **all** crossing atoms of its bounded source universe; thus it is an effective-update result for a preprocessed workload, not a uniform polylogarithmic total-input or unbounded-time theorem. Updating the rank tree separately at each affected atom can generate many persistent nodes; the proof gives an upper bound, not a memory-optimality result. The checker reports actual allocated node counts.

## 4. Theorem R113.3 — Single-edit capacity jump can be arbitrarily large

In the general finite ranked-source model, choose all sources to be eligible throughout `I`. Let `u_0 ≻ u_1 ≻ ... ≻ u_m ≻ u_{m+1}`, take `C={u_1,...,u_m}`, `F=C∪{u_{m+1}}`, `G=C`. The unique differing identity is `u_{m+1}`, so `K^*(I)=m`. Toggle `u_0` into `F` only. The highest differing identity is now `u_0`, and **`K^*(I)=0`**. Thus one identity edit can reduce the all-k capacity by an arbitrary prescribed integer `m`.

This is a sharp counterexample to an update rule that attempts to modify the single scalar capacity only by `±1` after an arbitrary one-sided edit. The complete rank/difference structure resolves the jump exactly. This construction requires no assertion about the density of S23 crossings. For an S23 same-time three-branch illustration, whenever its shared time eligibility is nonempty, set `C={(t,1)}`, `F=C∪{(t,0)}`, `G=C`, then toggle `(t,2)` into `F`; the pointwise capacity on an eligible atom drops from 1 to 0.

## 5. Exact executable verification and coverage

The attached `check_r113.py.gz.b64` decodes to the original Python 3 source, SHA256 `c3e28fb330154c0c23d76d60be4e03493fad1a5ba2e231e21421023ec7e87897`. Decode `base64 -d check_r113.py.gz.b64 | gzip -dc > check_r113.py` and run `python check_r113.py`.

The self-contained checker uses only the Python standard library, exact `fractions.Fraction`, source identities `(t,b)` for `-6≤t≤6`, `0≤b≤2`, `(j,x,a,c)=(0,1/4,0,1)`, and closed rational `I=[0,1]`. Eligibility is membership of `{x+(t-j)θ}` in the positive **half-open** fractional arc `[{aθ},{cθ})`, with directed-wrap handling and an empty arc when endpoints coincide. It computes the six affine integer-crossing families and checks every rational singleton or open-gap representative. History updates fork from randomly selected preserved roots, with seed `1132026`.

Observed deterministic check counts: 39 universe identities; 40 distinct interior cuts; 83 exact atoms; **480 one-sided historical edit steps**, creating 481 versions; **39,840 exact atom-capacity comparisons** against independent direct membership/list calculation; **1,440 cross-k direct Top-k checks**; **479 exact rational disagreement-witness tests**; 26 historical-root reuse checks. It allocated 115,090 rank-tree nodes and 139,805 atom-tree nodes under its explicit node-count model. This run took 1.7036 seconds on the current local runtime (a contextual measurement, not a portable performance guarantee). `verification_r113.json` contains raw metadata and counters; all assertions passed.

Tests cover the entire finite partition for **each of the generated history pairs**, not all possible pairs `F,G⊆U`. The proof of general finite-model correctness is structural and independent of the random trials. Exact-atom exhaustiveness relies on the stated six crossing-family argument already used in R112.

## 6. Next research unit R114

Combine this persistent rank index with **dynamically inserted/deleted crossing times**, including the reversible cut-support machinery of R111 and the rank-tail pruning of R112. Investigate persistent range updates for the common-only case, compression of identical atom rank-tree roots, and how much memory is actually saved under adversarial oscillation of the lowest/highest differing identity. Compare full construction plus membership-index cost, bit-operation cost, version retention, exact witnessing and alternate materialization baselines. Keep the native Heartbeat embedding/observer horizon separate until explicitly constructed and validated.
